what_it_does: This chip monitors chemicals in the body using 16 tiny sensors built into a millimeter-sized implant. Each sensor is an organic electrochemical transistor—a type of molecular switch that detects biomarkers by measuring tiny electrical changes when a target molecule binds to it. The chip reads all 16 channels wirelessly, avoiding the need for wires into the implant. This is smaller and simpler than older approaches like traditional three-electrode setups, which required separate reference and counter electrodes and didn't scale well to many channels.
